title: Greetings & Polite Expressions
objectives: Use common greetings for different times of day.
Use please, thank you, and excuse me appropriately.
canDo: I can greet people, say goodbye, and use basic polite expressions.

warmUp.title: Cumprimentos
warmUp.prompt: Como você cumprimenta alguém de manhã? À noite? Em português temos várias formas — em inglês também!
reflectionQuestions: What do you say in the morning?

explanation:
Greetings depend on time and formality.

Morning: Good morning! | Afternoon: Good afternoon! | Evening/night: Good evening! / Good night! (goodbye)

Informal: Hi! / Hello! / Hey!

Polite: Please | Thank you / Thanks | You're welcome | Excuse me | Sorry

Goodbye: Bye! / Goodbye! / See you later! / See you tomorrow!

grammar.title: Greetings & Politeness
grammar.rule: Good morning/afternoon/evening + name is friendly and polite. Good night is usually a farewell, not a greeting. Please goes before or after a request: Please help me. / Help me, please.

examples.sentence: Excuse me, is this seat free?

vocabulary.example: Excuse me, where is the bathroom?

reading.title: A Busy Morning
reading.text: At 8 a.m., Ana arrives at work. She says "Good morning!" to her colleague Tom. Tom says "Good morning, Ana!" At lunch, they say "Good afternoon!" to the new intern, Sofia. Sofia says "Nice to meet you!" At 6 p.m., Ana says "Goodbye, everyone! See you tomorrow!" Tom says "Bye, Ana! Have a good evening!"

questions.question: What does Ana say at 8 a.m.?
What does Sofia say when she meets people?
questions.explanation: Sofia says Nice to meet you!

questions.question: Does Ana say goodbye at 6 p.m.?
When do they say Good afternoon?
questions.explanation: At lunch they say Good afternoon!

writing.prompt: Write a short dialogue (6 lines) between two people meeting at a language school. Include a greeting, please/thank you, and goodbye.
writing.modelAnswer: A: Good morning! B: Good morning! A: Is this seat free, please? B: Yes, it is. A: Thank you! B: You're welcome. A: Goodbye! B: See you later!

tutorHints: Explain Good night = leaving, not arriving.
